what_it_does: Neuro-symbolic AI combines two styles of reasoning: a neural network that learns patterns from data, and a symbolic reasoner that applies explicit logical rules. These two parts have very different computational shapes — the neural side does dense matrix math, while the symbolic side manipulates graphs and logical expressions — so neither ordinary GPUs (designed for neural nets) nor traditional CPUs (designed for general logic) handle both well at once. NSFlow is a framework that targets FPGAs (chips whose internal wiring can be reconfigured after manufacture) to run neuro-symbolic workloads efficiently. It includes a tool that automatically analyzes how data flows through a neuro-symbolic program and generates a customized, parallel hardware layout tuned to that program's specific data dependencies. The reconfigurable FPGA fabric then provides flexible compute units and reorganizable memory that can be reshaped at runtime to match whichever part of the computation is active, with support for mixed numeric precisions (different levels of numerical detail) as needed.
